newsitem.title: USA: Chicago transit agency plans $25 mln cuts - papers.
newsitem.headline: Chicago transit agency plans $25 mln cuts - papers.

text.p: Chicago Transit Authority announced cuts in its late night bus and train services to save approximately $25 million per year, Chicago newspapers reported Friday.

The transit authority contends that the reorganization will affect three percent of the 1.4 million daily trips, but customers told the newspapers it would most heavily affect workers who depend most on public transportation.
In announcing the plans Thursday, CTA also said some buses could run more frequently during rush hours.
Even with the cuts, transit authority has projected a $37.6 million deficit in 1998 that will rise to $61.8 million if further action isn't taken, Chicago Tribune and Chicago Sun-Times reported.
